item.title: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG
item.description: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG According to Le Parisien (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), PSG are considering a move for Real Betis winger Ez Abde as they prepare to strengthen their attack in January, and Barcelona could benefit financially from the operation. The 24-year-old former Blaugrana attacker is among the names being evaluated by PSG and a transfer could see the Catalans receive a potential €12 million windfall. PSG eyeing Abde The current French and European champions have been hurt by injuries in the attacking department as two regular starters, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, have both suffered from ruptured ACLs, ruling them out for a long period. Luis Enrique & co. still have the likes of Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts as alternatives, while two former Barcelona stars, Ferran Torres and Ousmane Dembele, are also optons even though they have played centrally in recent seasons. Nonetheless, PSG are looking at the market to reinforce their attacking unit and Abde, who has excelled at Real Betis since leaving Barcelona, has emerged as an option. PSG interested in Abde. (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images) The Moroccan international is among several players that Les Parisiens are considering, including Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig and Chelsea youngster Estevao, among others. Barcelona, though, will be watching the situation closely, as Abde’s transfer could bring them a sizeable revenue boost. Why Barcelona stand to gain That is because, the Blaugrana still retain a 20% stake in the winger’s economic rights when he joined Real Betis permanently. With Abde’s release clause currently standing at €60 million, Barcelona would be entitled to €12 million if PSG triggered it in January. What is interesting is that, initially Barcelona had retained 50% of Abde’s rights when they sold him to Betis in the summer of 2023. Barcelona could benefit from Abde’s move to PSG (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, that arrangement changed in the winter window of 2025, when Los Verdiblancos acquired an additional 30% in exchange for terminating Vitor Roque’s loan agreement, allowing Barça to sell him to Palmeiras. Nonetheless, they still hold a significant financial interest in Abde’s future. A transfer at the full release-clause value would deliver a useful injection of revenue at a time when the club are looking for defensive reinforcements. However, as per the report, Real Betis are not believed to be particularly keen on selling the winger, which could complicate any approach from PSG. For now, Barcelona will be watching developments closely, knowing that a deal could bring them €12 million from a player who left the club three years ago.

item.description: Louisville football heads to Kentucky on Nov. 28 to compete in the annual Governor's Cup . Additionally, the Cardinals earned bragging rights for eliminating their rival from bowl eligibility. With the rich history between these two schools, you can test your knowledge here. Question 2: Which current Louisville Bats baseball coach scored a touchdown in the 1998 Governor's Cup? Question 3: What was 2016 Heisman Trophy winner Lamar Jackson's career record vs. Kentucky? Question 4 : Kentucky quarterback Tim Couch was the No. 1 overall pick in the 1999 NFL Draft. What was his career record vs. Louisville? Question 5: Who is the only player to rush for 100 or more yards three times in Governor's Cup history? Question 6 : Who holds the single-game record for most rushing yards in the Governor's Cup? item.title: These brother tandems team up one final time for Thanksgiving football
item.description: Brothers Brody and Danny Kenney started playing football together four years ago. “Brody convinced me to play,” said Danny, who was born a minute before Brody. On Wednesday, the 17-year-old twins from Leominster will suit up as seniors for St. Bernard’s in their final high school football game together during a Thanksgiving Eve tussle against Oakmont. “Playing with a twin has been nothing but the best,” said Danny, a wide receiver and safety who plays basketball in the winter. “I know I always have someone on my side looking out for me.” “It means a lot to (share) the field with Danny for our last Thanksgiving game,” said Brody, a tight end and linebacker who plays ice hockey in the winter. “I couldn’t be more thankful for having him by my side.” A day later, brothers Dean and Max Furcillo will share the football field for one last time during Nashoba’s Thanksgiving Day clash with Clinton. “It’s honestly special and rare,” said Max, a senior tight end who started playing football four years ago along with his younger sibling. “I’m going to look back on this forever.” “I want to end with a win for him,” said Dean, a sophomore quarterback. With a bunch of brother tandems (including a handful of twins) linking up on the gridiron this fall, the terrific trio of turkey, touchdowns and twinning is what’s on the menu for high school football teams across Central Mass. this Thanksgiving. So, the T&G caught up with a collection of varsity siblings to talk pigskin and turkey ahead of their holiday games. Bon appétit. Twinning Brothers Anthony and Tyrell Williams were excited to share the spotlight this season as a pair of senior running backs with the St. Bernard’s football team. But during the Bernardians’ first scrimmage on Sept. 1, Tyrell suffered a spinal compression fracture. “I honestly didn’t know if that (injury) was going to be the end of my season,” said Tyrell, who is 17 and was born three minutes after this twin brother. Luckily, Tyrell rejoined the Bernardians in time for their win over Oxford on Oct. 30. A week later, Anthony scored four rushing touchdowns while Tyrell caught a TD pass in a playoff victory over Easthampton. Tyrell then scored the game-tying touchdown with 31 seconds left to help St. Bernard’s beat Blue Hills, 21-20, on Nov. 13 to secure a spot in the Division 7 state semifinals. “I’m just grateful it healed over time and I’m back,” Tyrell told the T&G last week. “I was pumped up that I could play with my brother again.” “It's a blessing,” Anthony said. “I’m grateful.” Beyond the St. Bernard’s Kenney and Williams brothers, there are a trio of other twin tandems that teamed up in Central Mass. this fall. item.title: Todd McLellan excited about adding Kirby Dach to Red Wings lineup
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings anticipate newcomer Kirby Dach being in the lineup for their next game. That comes against the Vancouver Canucks at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday, Nov. 25 (7:30 p.m., Detroit SportsNet), giving Dach one practice and one morning skate to adjust to his new teammates. Dach was part of the haul the Wings acquired from the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday in the Dylan Larkin trade, the centerpiece of which was 20-year-old center Michael Hage, who plays for Michigan. While Hage is the future, Dach is the present. The 6-foot-4, 221-pound 25-year-old has posted 144 points in 328 career NHL games since being drafted No. 3 overall in 2019 by the Chicago Blackhawks . OFF THE HORCOFF: Wings interim GM on why he finally traded Dylan Larkin "I'm excited about getting him here," coach Todd McLellan said after Monday's practice. "He's a young man that was drafted really high and probably rushed into the league. We all do that with those kids, probably a little too quick and probably affected his confidence. But I've been watching him lately, and it looks like he's playing some of his better hockey." Dach was en route to Detroit on Monday afternoon, after getting his work visa in order. So was goaltender Sam Montembeault, also part of the trade, but he has been injured. How much Dach can help the Wings (who are 8-12-3 after losing eight of their past 10 games) remains to be seen, but at least he gives them some added depth down the middle. "I think he has a physical side of the game that he can add to our locker room and hopefully that could be beneficial," Moritz Seider said. "I think maybe he's excited for a little bit of a change-up. He can be a big player, tall, obviously a lot of skill, plays on the wing, on the center. So I think we're all excited for him to come here." As for finally being done with the Larkin saga – at least until he and his Canadiens visit LCA on Feb. 18 – players in the Wings locker room sounded relieved it was over. "As much as we've tried to compartmentalize and separate it, and I think we've done a pretty good job of that," Andrew Copp said, "you leave the rink and it's everywhere. It's as soon as you go to your phone, you got friends asking about it, that kind of thing. So I think we've done a really good job as a team, but it'll be nice to just move on from the whole situation." News of the trade broke Sunday evening, a little before 9 p.m. "I was sitting on my couch, and texts started flowing in pretty quickly," Copp said. "It's been out there for a long time, the trade request, that it's almost like there isn't a reaction. He's been separated from the team for a few weeks now, so that part has already happened. Publicly, it's already happened, he hasn't been in the room. We're adding a player, or two players to our team, and it's just kind of going from there." item.title: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026
item.description: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026 The award is staying in Leipzig! Nassim “Nassada” Dahman has been named eFootballer of the Year 2026 . The kicker editorial team voted the RBLZ new signing Germany’s best eFootballer of the year following his first nomination. He beat a field of nominees that also included two of his current teammates, Levy Finn Rieck and Alihan Hadzhi . It’s the sixth time that the award has gone to an RBLZ Gaming player. Dahman becomes the third RBLZ player to win it, following in the footsteps of Umut Gültekin (2020 to 2023) and Levy Finn Rieck (2025). A memorable year capped by a fourth-place finish in Paris Nassada laid the foundations for his success early in the season. He secured his place at the World Championship back in January by reaching the quarter-finals of the FC Pro Open in London. It was the first time that his club at the time, SC Freiburg, had qualified for the World Championship. Nassada was then crowned German champion in April . He came out on top against the best players in the Virtual Bundesliga at the individual championship, beating RBLZ player Alihan Hadzhi in a thrilling final. Dahman proved that he was among the world’s best at the FC Pro World Championship in July. He finished second in the league phase with 15 points from six games to qualify directly for the round of 16, where he recorded a 9-1 win. He then beat world number one and former RBLZ player Anders Vejrgang 11-5 in the quarter-finals. Defeats in the semi-finals and the third-place play-off meant he ultimately finished fourth out of the 36 best players in the world. Making an instant impact in Leipzig Nassada has wasted little time settling in at RBLZ Gaming. He and Alihan Hadzhi played a key role in the team’s victory at the first VBL Club Championship Offline Showdown at the Allianz Arena in Munich. In the round of 16 against Holstein Kiel, he came from 3-1 down to win his singles match 4-3 with a last-minute goal. In the final against SC Paderborn 07, his 8-6 win over Jonas “Jonny” Wirth in extra time secured a 12-11 aggregate victory. Nassim Dahman: “It’s a huge honour to be named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026. Having won the VBL title, I’m incredibly proud to round off the season with this award. Joining RBLZ Gaming was an important next step for me as I look to build on my success and win international titles with the team.” Nassada will be presented with the trophy on 14th November during the second VBL Club Championship Showdown at XPERION Berlin. item.title: Michigan basketball ready for return of Las Vegas vibes
item.description: For the first time since Jan. 27, 2025, Michigan men's basketball is not ranked. The Wolverines fell out of the USA TODAY Sports Men's Basketball Coaches Poll on Monday, Nov. 23, after their 79-73 loss to Villanova in Philadelphia on Saturday. The defeat was rough for the Wolverines, who shot 39.7% from the floor, 22.6% on 3s, turned the ball over more than twice as much as Villanova (16-7) and got just nine points from their reserves. The Wolverines spent the night in Philly recovering before flying directly to Las Vegas on Sunday, as they prepare for the Players Era 16 tournament. That begins with their fourth Big East opponent in six games this season, Creighton (4-1), on Tuesday (5:30 p.m., ESPN). FINDING ITS FOOTING: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed U-M is 1-2 already against the Big East, with losses to UConn and Villanova sandwiched around a win over Marquette. There is recent history to suggest U-M should be able to bounce back. Michigan is 5-0 in midseason tournaments over the past two seasons, going 2-0 in the Fort Myers Tip-Off in November 2024 and sweeping November 2025's Players Era Championship in historic fashion – three wins in three days by 100 points combined. Moreover, Michigan is 18-2 in all neutral-site tournaments – including, of course, 6-0 in this spring's 2026 NCAA Tournament – over the past two seasons. “It's been a pretty big part of what we believe has helped our teams become more connected,” coach Mike Boynton Jr. recently told reporters. “People do believe that translates into on-court success. There's no real science behind that, I don't think. But I do think that the teams that we've had the last few years have become closer on these road trips because we have spent that time together. "I do think there's an element of them trusting each other, feeling confident that they have each other's best interest on the court that's helping in games.” For many of this season's Wolverines, it's a new experience. Columbia transfer Kenny Noland, who called it "high level" hoops, said he remembers taking notice of the way U-M was "smacking" opponents in Las Vegas last year, even while he was in the Ivy League. For freshmen such as Quinn Costello, it's the first college tournament, a test on quick turnarounds and new environments. But for others, such as Elliott Cadeau, Trey McKenney and Roddy Gayle Jr., it's a chance to return to where U-M put the nation on notice a season ago (and earned $2 million for the program's NIL fund – $1 million for participating and $1 million for winning it). item.description: Jayden Paulino flashes a broad smile and says stars are nice, but winning is even better. “It all starts up front,” the Passaic Tech senior two-way lineman said after his team’s 41-16 win over Piscataway on Nov. 21. “You can’t win a game without a good offensive line. You can’t win a game without a good defensive line. I think we showed that.” On both lines for the Bulldogs is where you’ll find Paulino. The 6-foot-4, 270-pound athletic mountain is a catalyst for an offense that has produced almost 5,000 yards of total offense this season. Defensively he’s got 4.5 sacks and the second most tackles on the team at 83. “Jayden has Power 4 [college] offers as a defensive lineman and an offensive lineman,” said Bulldogs coach Matt Demarest. “I don’t know how many other kids in the state can say that.” And when you have a player like that, you don’t take him off the field. Even though he was smiling after the Bulldogs' win, he also looked tired. “I played a lot of football today man,” Paulino said. “But you know what, it’s fun, when you get to this level you want to be playing as much as you can. I just love all my guys. They are right with me.” Paulino, a Paterson product, got into playing football in third grade, and his favorite thing is the aggressiveness and going up against an opponent one on one. His older brother played receiver and defensive back for Passaic Tech. Jayden got the size. He also wrestled heavyweight for the Bulldogs last winter. “I got the good genes,” Jayden said smiling. “I am a big boy.” Jayden Paulino’s recruiting stock rises to four-star status Jayden gave a verbal commitment to play at Boston College this summer, but some new options have popped up. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino identifies January priority as Man Utd prepare move for Benjamin Sesko alternative
item.description: Liverpool v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Despite possessing the most porous defence across Europe's top five leagues after a heavy defeat at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino will prioritise signing a striker in January. Manchester United's summer gamble in attack has backfired due to injury, prompting the club to seek a reliable alternative ahead of the winter window. Pochettino ignores defence to prioritise January striker Pochettino will focus on recruiting a new forward rather than strengthening United's leaky defence in the January transfer window. Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool left United with the most porous backline in any of Europe's top five leagues. Michael Carrick's successor received an immediate reality check at Anfield, with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches. Despite those glaring defensive flaws, Pochettino views the opposite end of the pitch as an equal concern. The Red Devils opted against signing a forward during the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired. The club's hierarchy now has just over a month to identify attacking reinforcements before trading resumes. Injury crisis forces search for reliable forward United's attacking woes stem from a nagging shin injury suffered by Benjamin Sesko . The 23-year-old Slovenia international showed promise after a difficult start following his £74 million move from RB Leipzig last season, yet he has managed just six appearances this term. With Sesko unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest, Pochettino has alternated between Bryan Mbuemo and Matheus Cunha in central striking roles. Joshua Zirkzee remains largely untrusted to lead the line. According to The Times , Pochettino will seek a "more reliable option" to cover for Zirkzee as soon as the January window opens. Securing a dependable focal point is now paramount to lifting United out of danger. Anfield humiliation exposes United's severe defensive frailties Pochettino's decision to prioritise a striker comes despite a harrowing defensive display against Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side. The Argentine handed Matthijs de Ligt a surprise start, but the Netherlands international struggled against a lively attack while still returning from a long-term injury. Matters worsened when Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes at Anfield. Senior defenders Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also failed to impress under relentless pressure. Even with his rearguard leaking goals at an alarming rate, Pochettino believes adding firepower is the most pressing task for his struggling squad. As Lubbock-Cooper Liberty and Brock rolled through dominant regular seasons, this Thanksgiving-week matchup looked more and more likely. Now one of Class 4A Division II's contenders will bow out. The No. 3 Patriots remain unscathed, although last week's area playoff was tighter than projected. Monahans played tough before a 28-14 Liberty win. The game was tied at 7 at halftime. Patriots junior Kaiden Joseph ran for 225 yards and three touchdowns as he continued a torrid playoff pace. He notched 234 yards and four TDs in the first round against Burkburnett. Brock boasts an impressive resume itself. The second-ranked Eagles' lone loss is 38-27 at Anna, an undefeated 5A D-II squad prepping for its own regional semifinal. Among Brock's most impressive results is a 59-7 win over district foe Graham, which plays in the other Region I-4A D-II semifinal Friday. The Eagles enter off a 68-6 win over Big Spring. That continued a stretch of six consecutive games Brock has allowed seven points or fewer. The Eagles average 10.2 points allowed on the season. item.title: $250 scholarship to help Bloomington student try basketball
item.description: A $250 scholarship is helping a Fairview Elementary School fourth grader get a chance to try basketball through Bloomington Parks and Recreation. Ma'Siah Hanson received the fall Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship, according to a community announcement. Hanson plans to use the award to play Bloomington Youth Basketball at Twin Lakes Recreation Center in January. Hanson is a longtime participant in the Banneker Afterschool program and a member of the Fairview Chess Club. His athletic interests include gymnastics, martial arts and football, and he is eager to try basketball. The Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship provides two awards annually to Fairview Elementary students in the Banneker Afterschool program. Each $250 scholarship can help pay registration fees, equipment, uniforms and other gear needed to participate in a program through Bloomington Parks and Recreation or another local youth sports organization. Scholarship honors Don Shiflet's work with young athletes Shiflet's family established the scholarship after his death in 2019 to honor his commitment to helping young athletes and making sports more accessible to children in the community. Shiflet played a role in starting youth football and baseball programs in Bloomington and surrounding communities. He was inducted into the Monroe County Sports Hall of Fame in 2011 and was a charter member of the Bloomington Softball Hall of Fame. His involvement with the local softball community stretched back decades. Shiflet helped build Parks and Recreation's adult softball program beginning in 1952. The Lower Cascades North ball diamond was named Don Shiflet Field in 2001 in recognition of that service. He also spent 53 years working in sporting goods sales, providing athletic equipment to Indiana University and dozens of schools across Indiana. According to the announcement, family members said that Shiflet quietly helped young athletes whose families couldn't afford the equipment or clothing they needed to participate. "Don was known for never turning away someone in need, whether it be new shoes or a new glove or a pair of athletic shorts. His generosity was never forgotten by those he helped throughout the years," Kelsey Pearson, Fairview Elementary School assistant principal and Shiflet's granddaughter, said in the announcement. "One of Dad’s greatest joys was helping kids," Shiflet's daughter, Tammy Brannon, said in the announcement. "He was always willing to help kids out, especially those who might not otherwise have the opportunity to participate." Brannon said that her father had a special place in his heart for children involved in programming at Banneker Community Center. His family wanted the scholarship to reflect his kindness, generosity and love of youth sports. "Our family could not think of a better way to carry on his legacy than through setting up a scholarship to benefit local youth wanting to play sports," Pearson said in the announcement. item.description: Suits and ties at the tailgate. Famous coaches and players. Cheerleaders, twirlers, mascots and generations of Clemson and South Carolina fans. Photos spanning the 1940s through 2025 offer a visual journey through more than eight decades of the rivalry, capturing how one of South Carolina’s biggest sports traditions changed while its intensity endured. Among the earliest images is an aerial view of the parking lot at the 1949 game, a scene frozen in time more than 75 years ago. Other photos connect the rivalry to history beyond football. The 1963 game, originally scheduled for Nov. 23, was postponed after the assassination of President John F. Kennedy and played on Thanksgiving Day. Clemson won 24-20. U.S. Sen. Strom Thurmond attended the 1965 game. The gallery also traces the coaches and players who defined different eras. Clemson’s Frank Howard and South Carolina’s Paul Dietzel appear in earlier years, followed by Clemson’s Danny Ford and South Carolina’s Joe Morrison. Later matchups featured Clemson’s Tommy Bowden against Lou Holtz and Dabo Swinney against Steve Spurrier. More recent images include Clemson quarterbacks Deshaun Watson, Trevor Lawrence, and Cade Klubnik, as well as South Carolina coaches Will Muschamp and Shane Beamer. But the famous faces are only part of the story. Packed stands, spirited tailgaters and fans dressed in orange or garnet reveal how generations made this rivalry their own. The cars, clothes, coaches and players changed. The passion endured, creating a visual history of Clemson-Carolina from the 1940s to 2025 across South Carolina. item.title: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
item.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen . And given that the grand prix had turned into what can only be described as a slipstreaming battle of the kind normally associated with track cycling, it was almost inevitable that Hadjar would sooner or later have a go at taking the lead. But a reminder from his race engineer Richard Wood was not long in coming. The priority, Wood explained, was to avoid losing time as a team. Red Bull needed to build a gap to George Russell , rather than waste precious seconds fighting among themselves. And Hadjar, certainly no stranger to self-confidence but ultimately a loyal Red Bull team player, complied. Eventually, he found himself alongside Verstappen again on the long straight towards Turn 14. But the Dutchman had no intention of surrendering the lead without a fight. "Can he stop defending? Otherwise I just gotta lose time," Hadjar complained over the radio. Wood, however, stuck to the plan they had already agreed upon: "Team request is to defend against George, otherwise we will be yo-yoing." At that point, Russell was the closest pursuer of the Red Bull Express at the front, with the trio merrily swapping positions. On one occasion, Russell even managed to overtake both Red Bulls simultaneously, only to find himself back in third place two or three corners later. In Las Vegas, slipstreaming and energy management were powerful weapons. More powerful, in fact, than outright speed. Hadjar's radio messages made it clear that, from a team perspective, he would have preferred something resembling a rotating paceline in cycling over conventional formation driving: a group of riders works together by constantly rotating the lead, allowing each member to benefit from the slipstream and enabling the group as a whole to travel faster than an individual rider could manage alone. But Red Bull, apparently caught somewhat off guard by the peculiar dynamics of the race, did not seem particularly interested in Hadjar's proposal. The idea of sharing the lead in order to open up a gap to Russell was not even discussed with Verstappen. At least, there is no corresponding question to be heard on the Dutchman's official onboard radio feed. Malone, now the 55-year-old coach of the North Carolina men’s basketball program, started his high school career at Bishop Hendricken High School while his father, Brendan, was the head coach at Rhode Island. When Brendan Malone accepted an assistant coaching role with Hubie Brown and the NBA’s New York Knicks in 1986, Michael transferred to Seton Hall Prep for his final two seasons. MALONE'S START: UNC basketball coach Michael Malone didn't want the game ball, then he saw Roy Williams UNC'S BANNER WORLD: Michael Malone embracing pressure of UNC basketball and its banners And so began the back-and-forth battle with Farrell, who coached the Pirates for 34 seasons before retiring at the end of the 2010-11 season. item.description: FAYETTEVILLE — Peer pressure got Amere Brown to Arkansas basketball . A love for the community and a desire to carve his own path is keeping Brown in the northwest corner of the state for the foreseeable future. Brown followed his best friend, Meleek Thomas, to the Razorbacks ' program. He officially joined the roster on May 28, 2025. He was a 3-star recruit and an unheralded walk-on who was initially viewed as filler for an Arkansas roster that only brought in 10 to 12 players who seriously fought for minutes in each of John Calipari's first two seasons. Now, the 5-foot-9 guard is social-media rockstar with more than 600,000 followers on TikTok. His personality has clicked with the fan base and turned Brown into a crowd favorite. There are regular "Amere Brown" chants any time the Hogs are in the midst of a blowout victory on their own court. Fans clamor for playing time. What they don't see is the influence Brown has become in the Arkansas locker room. "Amere is the type of personality, the character that's a leader. He opens himself up to the other players. He's engaging with them," Arkansas associate head coach Kenny Payne said. "You can see when people are in that position, you're trying to figure out what's your space. To me, his space is leadership. His space is players trusting his friendship and brotherhood." Amere Brown's bond with Meleek Thomas led him to Arkansas basketball Brown met Thomas at an open gym when they were in fifth grade. Brown's dad would rent out gyms in Pittsburgh so talent across the city could come play pick-up games for free. The relationship eventually became what it is today, with Brown considering Thomas a third brother. Thomas told Brown throughout the recruiting process that he wanted the duo to spend their freshman years together. Thomas always had his eye on being a one-and-done college player, but he would tell coaches vying for his services that he hoped they could spare a walk-on spot for his friend. At first, Brown was hesitant. He aspired to play Division II football as a slot receiver. He also played defensive back in high school and went on a handful of recruiting visits for his own collegiate career. "I never wanted to be looked at as (Thomas') wingman," Brown said. "He wanted me to come with him on his visits, but I wanted him to handle that on his own. I was still pretty sure I was going to be playing football." By the time Signing Day rolled around in 2025, Brown still hadn't decided on a future home, and Thomas was still in his ear about joining the Razorbacks. Brown admits one of the biggest obstacles in his journey to Fayetteville was belief in his spot on the team. His dad jumped on a phone call with Calipari — who grew up just 17 miles outside of downtown Pittsburgh in Moon Township — and Brown was finally comfortable with committing his future to the Hall of Fame coach. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
